Definition: from G4012 and G2192; to hold all around, i.e. include, clasp (figuratively):--+ astonished, contain, after (this manner).
BiblicalUsage: Periecho means to hold around, to contain — and by extension, to be astonished. Peter says it is contained in the Scripture that God lays a chief corner stone in Sion, and the fishermen were astonished at the draught of fishes they had taken.
TheologicalSignificance: What I believe is that what is contained in Scripture is certain: the cornerstone is laid in Sion, and the fishermen's astonishment is the right response to it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
